lesson.u00-sample.title: Sample: Capture
lesson.u00-sample.s1: The empty points next to a stone are its liberties (气 qì). This white stone has just one.
lesson.u00-sample.s2: Black fills the last liberty. The white stone is captured (提子 tízǐ) and removed.
lesson.u00-sample.s3: Stones that touch form a group and share their liberties. Fill the last one and the whole group is captured.
lesson.u00-sample.e1.prompt: Tap the last liberty of the white stone.
lesson.u00-sample.e1.hint: Look at the four points around the white stone: only one is empty.
lesson.u00-sample.e2.prompt: Tap all the liberties of the black stone, then press Check.
lesson.u00-sample.e2.hint: Only the points straight up, down, left and right count — not diagonals.
lesson.u00-sample.e3.hint: It has one liberty left. Fill it.
lesson.u00-sample.e3.explain: The stone had no liberties left, so it was captured.
lesson.u00-sample.e4.prompt: Connect the two black stones into one group.
lesson.u00-sample.e4.hint: Which point touches both black stones?
lesson.u00-sample.e5.prompt: Can Black capture the white stone with one move?
lesson.u00-sample.e5.w1: After A the stone still has a liberty at B.
lesson.u00-sample.e5.w2: After B the stone still has a liberty at A.
lesson.u00-sample.e5.explain: One move fills only one liberty; here two must be filled.
lesson.u00-sample.e6.prompt: How many liberties does the marked black group have?
lesson.u00-sample.e6.hint: Count the empty points touching either black stone, each only once.
lesson.u01-board.title: Board and stones
lesson.u01-board.s1: Stones go on the crossing points (交叉点 jiāochādiǎn) of the board (棋盘 qípán), not in squares. Letters = columns, numbers = rows: c3.
lesson.u01-board.s2: Black (黑 hēi) always plays first, then White (白 bái). The players take turns, one stone each time.
lesson.u01-board.s3: A stone (棋子 qízǐ) never moves once it is placed. It stays there until it is captured, which you will learn soon.
lesson.u01-board.e1.prompt: Tap the crossing marked with a triangle.
lesson.u01-board.e1.hint: Tap exactly where two lines cross.
lesson.u01-board.e2.hint: c is the third column from the left, 4 the fourth row from the bottom.
lesson.u01-board.e3.prompt: Black plays first. Place a black stone on d2.
lesson.u01-board.e4.w2: Black just played; the turn passes.
lesson.u01-board.e4.prompt: Black has just played. Whose turn is it now?
lesson.u01-board.e4.explain: The players alternate, so White follows Black.
lesson.u01-board.e5.prompt: It is White's turn. Place a white stone on b3.
lesson.u01-board.e5.hint: Column b, row 3, just left of the black stone.
lesson.u01-board.e6.o2: It may move one step per turn
lesson.u01-board.e6.w2: A stone cannot move after it is placed.
lesson.u01-board.e6.w3: You cannot take a placed stone back.
lesson.u01-board.e6.prompt: The black stone is on c3. As the game goes on, what happens to it?
lesson.u01-board.e6.explain: A placed stone does not move; it stays on c3.
lesson.u01-board.e7.prompt: Tap all the white stones, then press Check.
lesson.u01-board.e7.hint: White stones are the light ones; there are three.
lesson.u02-liberties.title: Liberties
lesson.u02-liberties.s1: The empty points right next to a stone (up, down, left, right) are its liberties (气 qì). This stone has 4.
lesson.u02-liberties.s2: On an edge there is one neighbour less: only 3 liberties.
lesson.u02-liberties.s3: In a corner there are only 2. Diagonal points (crossed) never count.
lesson.u02-liberties.s4: An enemy stone takes a liberty away: after White plays c4, this stone has only 3.
lesson.u02-liberties.e1.prompt: Tap all the liberties of the black stone, then press Check.
lesson.u02-liberties.e1.hint: Look at the four points: up, down, left, right.
lesson.u02-liberties.e2.prompt: How many liberties does the black stone have?
lesson.u02-liberties.e2.hint: It is on the edge, so it has one neighbour less.
lesson.u02-liberties.e3.prompt: Tap all the liberties of the corner stone, then press Check.
lesson.u02-liberties.e3.hint: The diagonal point is not a liberty.
lesson.u02-liberties.e4.prompt: How many liberties does the black stone have left?
lesson.u02-liberties.e4.hint: Count only empty neighbours; points with a white stone do not count.
lesson.u02-liberties.e5.w1: A is in the open: 4 liberties.
lesson.u02-liberties.e5.w2: B is on an edge: 3 liberties.
lesson.u02-liberties.e5.prompt: Which black stone has the fewest liberties?
lesson.u02-liberties.e5.explain: A has 4 liberties, B has 3, and C in the corner has only 2.
lesson.u02-liberties.e6.prompt: Tap the last liberty of the black stone.
lesson.u02-liberties.e6.hint: Three neighbours hold white stones; one is empty.
lesson.u02-liberties.e7.prompt: White to play. Place a stone next to the black stone to take one of its liberties.
lesson.u02-liberties.e7.hint: Choose an empty point up, down, left or right of it.
lesson.u02-liberties.e8.prompt: How many liberties does the black stone have?
lesson.u02-liberties.e8.hint: Diagonal white stones take no liberty.
lesson.u02-liberties.e8.explain: Diagonal stones do not matter, so it still has 4 liberties.
lesson.u03-connection.title: Connection
lesson.u03-connection.s1: Stones touching up, down, left or right are connected (连接 liánjiē): one group (一块棋 yíkuàiqí) sharing its liberties, 6 here.
lesson.u03-connection.s2: Diagonal neighbours are not connected: these are two separate stones, with 4 liberties each.
lesson.u03-connection.s3: Play on d3 and the two stones become one group.
lesson.u03-connection.e1.w2: They touch, so they are already connected.
lesson.u03-connection.e1.prompt: Are these two black stones one group or two?
lesson.u03-connection.e1.explain: They touch top to bottom, so they are one group.
lesson.u03-connection.e2.w1: Diagonal contact is not a connection.
lesson.u03-connection.e2.prompt: Are these two black stones one group or two?
lesson.u03-connection.e2.explain: They only touch diagonally, so they are two groups.
lesson.u03-connection.e3.w1: Pair A has an empty point between its stones.
lesson.u03-connection.e3.prompt: Which pair of black stones is one group?
lesson.u03-connection.e3.hint: Look for the two that touch side to side or top to bottom.
lesson.u03-connection.e3.explain: Only pair C touches top to bottom.
lesson.u03-connection.e4.prompt: How many liberties does the marked black group have?
lesson.u03-connection.e4.hint: Count the empty points touching either stone, each only once.
lesson.u03-connection.e4.explain: Connected stones share liberties, so count the whole group: 5.
lesson.u03-connection.e5.prompt: Black to play. Connect the two black stones into one group.
lesson.u03-connection.e5.hint: Which point touches both black stones?
lesson.u03-connection.e5.explain: c3 touches both stones, so they became one group.
lesson.u03-connection.e6.prompt: Black to play. Connect the two diagonal black stones.
lesson.u03-connection.e6.hint: c2 is taken by White; try the other point that touches both.
lesson.u03-connection.e7.prompt: Tap every black stone in the same group as the marked stone, then press Check.
lesson.u03-connection.e7.hint: Follow only up, down, left, right; never diagonals.
lesson.u03-connection.e7.explain: b4 touches c3 only diagonally, so it is not in the group.
lesson.u04-capture.title: Capture
lesson.u04-capture.s1: This white stone has just one liberty left, on c4.
lesson.u04-capture.s2: Black fills the last liberty. A stone with no liberties is captured (提子 tízǐ) and removed from the board.
lesson.u04-capture.s3: In a corner it is easier: two black stones are enough.
lesson.u04-capture.s4: When a group is captured, all its stones come off together, however many there are.
lesson.u04-capture.e1.hint: It has one liberty left. Fill it.
lesson.u04-capture.e1.explain: The stone had no liberties left, so it was captured.
lesson.u04-capture.e2.prompt: Capture the white stone on the edge.
lesson.u04-capture.e2.hint: Black is already left and right of c1; only the point above is open.
lesson.u04-capture.e3.prompt: Capture the white stone in the corner.
lesson.u04-capture.e3.hint: A corner stone has two liberties; one is already taken.
lesson.u04-capture.e4.w1: The white stone still has a liberty on c3.
lesson.u04-capture.e4.o2: No, it still has a liberty
lesson.u04-capture.e4.prompt: Black plays on A. Is the white stone captured?
lesson.u04-capture.e4.explain: c3 is still empty, so the white stone keeps one liberty and is not captured.
lesson.u04-capture.e5.prompt: Capture both white stones with one move.
lesson.u04-capture.e5.hint: The two white stones are one group. Where is its last liberty?
lesson.u04-capture.e5.explain: Filling the shared last liberty captured the whole group.
lesson.u04-capture.e6.prompt: Tap the point where Black can capture a stone.
lesson.u04-capture.e6.hint: Find the white stone with only one liberty.
lesson.u04-capture.e6.explain: The corner stone has two liberties; the stone on c4 has only c3.
lesson.u04-capture.e7.prompt: Black to play. Find the move that captures.
lesson.u04-capture.e7.hint: Which white stone has only one liberty?
lesson.u04-capture.e7.explain: d5 was the last liberty of d4; b6 still has 3.
lesson.u04-capture.e8.prompt: Black plays on A. How many white stones are captured?
lesson.u04-capture.e8.hint: A is the last liberty of the whole white group.
lesson.u04-capture.e8.explain: The three white stones are one group and A is its last liberty.
lesson.u05-atari.title: Atari and escape
lesson.u05-atari.s1: Black plays d3 and White has one liberty left. This warning is atari (叫吃 jiàochī): next turn Black can capture.
lesson.u05-atari.s2: Your stone is in atari. You can extend (长 zhǎng): add a stone on the free liberty. Now the group has 3 liberties.
lesson.u05-atari.s3: Count first! Here the extension leaves only one liberty (c5): still in atari, no escape.
lesson.u05-atari.s4: Another way: capture the stone that attacks yours. Black takes b3 and c3 gets a new liberty.
lesson.u05-atari.e1.prompt: Put the white stone in atari: leave it just one liberty.
lesson.u05-atari.e1.hint: It has two liberties. Fill one of them.
lesson.u05-atari.e1.explain: The stone has one liberty left and can be captured next.
lesson.u05-atari.e2.w1: A still has b4 and c5.
lesson.u05-atari.e2.w3: B has one liberty: it is in atari.
lesson.u05-atari.e2.prompt: Which white stone is in atari?
lesson.u05-atari.e2.explain: B has only e4 left; A still has two liberties.
lesson.u05-atari.e3.prompt: The black stone is in atari. Tap its last liberty.
lesson.u05-atari.e3.hint: Three neighbours hold white stones; find the empty one.
lesson.u05-atari.e4.prompt: The black stone is in atari. Extend to make it escape.
lesson.u05-atari.e4.explain: After extending, the group has 3 liberties and is safe.
lesson.u05-atari.e5.prompt: The black stone on the edge is in atari. Make it escape.
lesson.u05-atari.e5.hint: It can only extend towards a4.
lesson.u05-atari.e6.o1: Yes, it has two or more liberties
lesson.u05-atari.e6.o2: No, it still has one liberty
lesson.u05-atari.e6.prompt: Black extends on A. Has the black group escaped?
lesson.u05-atari.e6.explain: After c4 only c5 is left, so it is still in atari.
lesson.u05-atari.e7.prompt: Put the white group in atari.
lesson.u05-atari.e7.hint: The white group has two liberties. Fill one.
lesson.u05-atari.e7.explain: The connected stones share liberties; only one is left.
lesson.u05-atari.e8.prompt: Black's c3 is in atari. Rescue it by capturing a white stone.
lesson.u05-atari.e8.hint: Which white stone has only one liberty?
lesson.u05-atari.e8.explain: After capturing d3, c3 has liberties again and is safe.
lesson.u05-review.title: Review
lesson.u05-review.e1.prompt: How many liberties does the black stone have?
lesson.u05-review.e2.prompt: How many separate black groups are on the board?
lesson.u05-review.e2.hint: Diagonal contact is not a connection.
lesson.u05-review.e2.explain: c6 and d5 touch only diagonally, so there are 3 groups.
lesson.u05-review.e3.prompt: Black to play. Connect the two black stones.
lesson.u05-review.e3.hint: Which point lies between the two black stones?
lesson.u05-review.e4.prompt: Capture both white stones with one move.
lesson.u05-review.e4.hint: Find the only empty point next to the white group.
lesson.u05-review.e5.prompt: Put the white group in atari.
lesson.u05-review.e5.hint: The white group has two liberties. Fill one.
lesson.u05-review.e6.prompt: The black stone on the edge is in atari. Make it escape.
lesson.u05-review.e7.prompt: Tap all the liberties of the marked black group, then press Check.
lesson.u05-review.e7.hint: The two stones share liberties; tap each point once.
lesson.u05-review.e8.w2: B is far from the group and takes no liberty.
lesson.u05-review.e8.w3: C is far from the group and takes no liberty.
lesson.u05-review.e8.prompt: Where can Black play to capture the white stones?
lesson.u05-review.e8.explain: The last liberty of the white group is d2.

fb.tapAll.extra: The points in red are not right — they were removed.
fb.pm.noCapture: Nothing was captured. A group is captured only when its last liberty is filled.
fb.pm.captureTooFew: Only {{n}} captured — this exercise needs more.
fb.pm.noAtari: No enemy group is down to one liberty yet.
fb.pm.notConnected: The two stones are still separate groups.
fb.pm.stillAtari: The group still has only one liberty, so it can still be captured.
fb.pm.wrongPoint: That is not the point asked for.
fb.pm.selfAtari: Careful: your new stone has only one liberty left too.

lesson.u06-capture-go.title: Capture Go
lesson.u06-capture-go.s1: In Capture Go (吃子棋 chīzǐqí) the first player to capture the set number of stones wins. Here it is 1: Black plays c2 and wins.
lesson.u06-capture-go.s2: You play Black and move first; the bot plays White. Guard your own stones too: here White plays c4 and captures.
lesson.u06-capture-go.s3: Games 2 and 3 start with four stones, each with two liberties. Be the first to put an enemy stone in atari.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e1.prompt: Capture the white stone to win.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e1.hint: The white stone has one liberty left. Fill it.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e1.explain: You filled the last liberty, so the stone was captured.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e2.prompt: The first to capture 1 stone wins.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e2.hint: Each white stone has two liberties. Take one away to put it in atari.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e2.explain: Putting a stone in atari first made the bot defend.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e3.prompt: The first to capture 2 stones wins.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e3.hint: Atari the bot, but count your own stones' liberties too.
lesson.u06-capture-go.e3.explain: You captured two stones before the bot did.
lesson.u06-checkpoint.title: Capture Go games
lesson.u06-checkpoint.e1.prompt: 7×7 board. The first to capture 2 stones wins.
lesson.u06-checkpoint.e1.hint: Count both sides' liberties before you play.
lesson.u06-checkpoint.e1.explain: Counting liberties let you capture first.
lesson.u06-checkpoint.e2.prompt: You play White; the bot moves first. The first to capture 3 stones wins.
lesson.u06-checkpoint.e2.hint: Look at the bot's move first, then decide: attack or defend.
lesson.u06-checkpoint.e2.explain: It works as White too: count liberties, atari first.

lesson.u07-forbidden.title: Forbidden points
lesson.u07-forbidden.s1: Black playing on c3 would leave the stone with no liberty. That point is forbidden (禁入点 jìnrùdiǎn): you can't play there.
lesson.u07-forbidden.s2: One exception: a move that captures is allowed. At a1 Black takes the last liberty of both white stones and removes them.
lesson.u07-forbidden.s3: The rule holds for groups. e1 is the only liberty of the two black stones: Black may not play it, but White may and captures them.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e1.prompt: Black to play. Tap the point where Black may not play.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e1.hint: Look for an empty point with a white stone on every side.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e1.explain: c3 is surrounded by White: a stone there would have no liberty and capture nothing.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e2.prompt: Black to play. Tap the point where Black may not play.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e2.hint: A corner point has only two neighbours.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e2.explain: Both neighbours of a1, a2 and b1, are White: a stone there would have no liberty.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e3.w2: Black takes the last liberty of c4, so c4 is captured and c3 gets a liberty.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e3.explain: A move that captures is not forbidden.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e4.w1: The white stones still have liberties (c1 and e3), so nothing is captured and e1 would have no liberty.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e4.explain: Nothing is captured and the stone has no liberty: a forbidden point.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e5.prompt: Capture both white stones with one move.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e5.hint: Where is the one liberty both white stones share?
lesson.u07-forbidden.e5.explain: e5 looks forbidden, but it captures both white stones.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e6.prompt: Tap every point where Black may not play, then press Check.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e6.hint: There are three, each one enclosed by White stones.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e6.explain: a1, d4 and g7 are enclosed by White stones that all still have liberties.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e7.w1: a1 is the last liberty of the black stones: filling it leaves the whole group with none, and no white stone is captured.
lesson.u07-forbidden.e7.explain: The black group has one liberty, a1; filling it yourself is forbidden.
lesson.u08-ko.title: Ko
lesson.u08-ko.s1: Black plays c3 and captures c4. Now the stone on c3 has only one liberty: c4.
lesson.u08-ko.s2: Retaking on c4 at once could repeat forever. This is ko (打劫 dǎjié): you may not retake right away. Play elsewhere first.
lesson.u08-ko.s3: White ataris f6: a ko threat (劫材 jiécái). Black answers, the position has changed, and White may retake on c4.
lesson.u08-ko.e1.prompt: Black just captured (marked stone). Tap the point White may not play right now.
lesson.u08-ko.e1.hint: Retaking there would repeat the earlier position.
lesson.u08-ko.e1.explain: c4 is the ko point: White must play elsewhere first.
lesson.u08-ko.e2.prompt: Black just captured by playing b3. May White play on A right now?
lesson.u08-ko.e2.w1: A would capture b3 and bring back the position from before Black's move. Ko forbids that.
lesson.u08-ko.e2.explain: White must play elsewhere first, then may retake on a3.
lesson.u08-ko.e3.prompt: Black to play. Capture a white stone to start a ko.
lesson.u08-ko.e3.hint: Which white stone has only one liberty?
lesson.u08-ko.e3.explain: After taking c4, Black's c3 has one liberty and White cannot retake at once: a ko.
lesson.u08-ko.e4.prompt: Black just captured on c3. Why can't White play A?
lesson.u08-ko.e4.w1: Not a ko: Black's c2-c3 group has 4 liberties, so a white stone there could not capture it.
lesson.u08-ko.e4.o2: Because it is a forbidden point
lesson.u08-ko.e4.explain: A white stone on A would have no liberty and capture nothing: a forbidden point, not a ko.
lesson.u08-ko.e5.prompt: Black captured on c3, then White played e5 and Black played a5. May White play on A now?
lesson.u08-ko.e5.o2: No, it is still a ko
lesson.u08-ko.e5.w2: The ban lasts one turn only. Both sides have played elsewhere, so the position is different.
lesson.u08-ko.e5.explain: After moves elsewhere, White may retake on c4.
lesson.u08-ko.e6.prompt: White can't retake c4 yet. Play a move elsewhere that puts a black group in atari.
lesson.u08-ko.e6.hint: The black stone on f6 has two liberties: g6 and f7.
lesson.u08-ko.e6.explain: Black must answer or lose f6. Then the position has changed and White may retake on c4.
lesson.u08-ko.e7.prompt: White played g6 (atari) and Black answered f7. What may White do now?
lesson.u08-ko.e7.w2: No need: after Black's answer the position has changed.
lesson.u08-ko.e7.o3: Capture the black stones with g7
lesson.u08-ko.e7.w3: The black stones f6-f7 still have two liberties, e7 and g7.
lesson.u08-ko.e7.explain: The ko threat forced an answer, so White may retake.
lesson.u09-ladder.title: Ladder
lesson.u09-ladder.s1: Black ataris, White extends, Black ataris again… Chasing like this is a ladder (征子 zhēngzi).
lesson.u09-ladder.s2: The chase ends at the edge: White has nowhere to run and Black captures all four stones.
lesson.u09-ladder.s3: If a white stone waits ahead, White's extension joins it. The group gets 3 liberties and the ladder fails.
lesson.u09-ladder.e1.prompt: Black ataried and White extended to d3. How many liberties does the white group have now?
lesson.u09-ladder.e1.hint: Count the empty points next to c3 and d3.
lesson.u09-ladder.e1.explain: Only e3 and d4: Black can atari again.
lesson.u09-ladder.e2.prompt: To chase the white stone in a ladder, where should Black atari first?
lesson.u09-ladder.e2.w2: After B, White extends to c4 and has 3 liberties: the chase stops.
lesson.u09-ladder.e2.explain: A drives White toward the edge, atari after atari.
lesson.u09-ladder.e3.prompt: Keep chasing: put the white group in atari again.
lesson.u09-ladder.e3.hint: The white group has two liberties. Play on one of them.
lesson.u09-ladder.e3.explain: Atari again. White must keep extending, closer to the edge.
lesson.u09-ladder.e4.prompt: White has run to the edge. Capture the whole white group.
lesson.u09-ladder.e4.hint: The white group has only one liberty.
lesson.u09-ladder.e4.explain: e5 captures four stones: the ladder works.
lesson.u09-ladder.e5.prompt: Black ataris at c4 and keeps chasing. Will the ladder capture White?
lesson.u09-ladder.e5.w1: The white stone on e5 waits ahead: at e4 White joins it and has 3 liberties.
lesson.u09-ladder.e5.explain: The white stone ahead breaks the ladder.
lesson.u09-ladder.e6.prompt: This ladder will fail. Tap the white stone that lets White escape.
lesson.u09-ladder.e6.hint: Follow White's running path: which white stone is on it?
lesson.u09-ladder.e6.explain: The white stone on f5 is on the path: White joins it and the ladder fails.
lesson.u09-ladder.e7.prompt: Black ataris at e6 and keeps chasing. Will the ladder capture White?
lesson.u09-ladder.e7.w2: Nothing waits ahead: the chase runs into the corner and White runs out of liberties.
lesson.u09-ladder.e7.explain: The ladder runs to the edge and White is captured.
lesson.u09-ladder.e8.prompt: Chase the white stone all the way and capture it.
lesson.u09-ladder.e8.hint: Atari every time, driving White toward the edge.
lesson.u09-ladder.e8.explain: The ladder works: atari after atari, and White is captured at the edge. Sometimes two ataris work.
lesson.u09-ladder.e9.prompt: This ladder runs into the corner. Chase and capture.
lesson.u09-ladder.e9.hint: Start with the atari that drives White toward the corner.
lesson.u09-ladder.e9.explain: In the corner White has no way out and is captured.
lesson.u09-review.title: Review 2
lesson.u09-review.e1.prompt: Black to play. Tap the point where Black may not play.
lesson.u09-review.e1.hint: Look for an empty point with a white stone on every side.
lesson.u09-review.e1.explain: b3 is surrounded by White: a black stone there would have no liberty.
lesson.u09-review.e2.w2: a5 takes the last liberty of a4 and b5: both white stones are captured.
lesson.u09-review.e2.explain: A move that captures is not forbidden.
lesson.u09-review.e3.prompt: Black just captured by playing d3. May White play on A right now?
lesson.u09-review.e3.w1: A would capture d3 and bring back the position from before Black's move. Ko forbids that.
lesson.u09-review.e3.explain: White must play elsewhere first, then may retake on e3.
lesson.u09-review.e4.prompt: How many liberties does the marked black group have?
lesson.u09-review.e4.hint: The two stones share liberties; count each empty point once.
lesson.u09-review.e5.prompt: Put the white stone in atari.
lesson.u09-review.e5.hint: It has two liberties. Fill one of them.
lesson.u09-review.e5.explain: The stone has one liberty left and can be captured next.
lesson.u09-review.e6.hint: Which liberty does it have left?
lesson.u09-review.e6.explain: Black fills b3, the last liberty, and the white stone is captured.
lesson.u09-review.e7.prompt: To chase the white stone in a ladder, where should Black atari first?
lesson.u09-review.e7.w2: After B, White extends to c4 and has 3 liberties: the chase stops.
lesson.u09-review.e7.explain: A drives White toward the edge, atari after atari.
lesson.u09-review.e8.prompt: Black ataris at e4 and keeps chasing. Will the ladder capture White?
lesson.u09-review.e8.w1: The white stone on c5 waits ahead: at c4 White joins it and has 3 liberties.
lesson.u09-review.e8.explain: The white stone ahead breaks the ladder.
lesson.u09-review.e9.prompt: This time White runs downward. Chase and capture.
lesson.u09-review.e9.hint: Atari from the side that drives White toward the edge.
lesson.u09-review.e9.explain: The ladder works again: atari to the edge, then capture.

lesson.u10-eyes.title: Eyes
lesson.u10-eyes.s1: An empty point enclosed by one group's own stones is an eye (眼 yǎn). White cannot play there: it would have no liberty.
lesson.u10-eyes.s2: Here a white stone sits on the diagonal. b1 has one liberty: White c1 captures it. A false eye (假眼 jiǎyǎn).
lesson.u10-eyes.s3: If the diagonal points of an eye are your own stones, it is a real eye (真眼 zhēnyǎn). The diagonal of a1 is b2, Black's.
lesson.u10-eyes.e1.hint: Look for an empty point with only black stones around it.
lesson.u10-eyes.e1.explain: c1 is enclosed by Black: White cannot play there.
lesson.u10-eyes.e2.prompt: Is the marked point a1 a real or a false eye?
lesson.u10-eyes.e2.w2: The diagonal b2 is Black's own stone, so White cannot get in: it is a real eye.
lesson.u10-eyes.e2.explain: a1 is a real eye: White cannot play there.
lesson.u10-eyes.e3.prompt: Is the marked point c1 a real or a false eye?
lesson.u10-eyes.e3.w1: White c1 captures b1, which has one liberty, so c1 is a false eye.
lesson.u10-eyes.e3.explain: White can capture on c1, so it is a false eye.
lesson.u10-eyes.e4.prompt: Which is the real eye, A or B?
lesson.u10-eyes.e4.w2: White e1 captures d1, which has one liberty, so B is a false eye.
lesson.u10-eyes.e4.explain: A is a real eye and B is a false eye.
lesson.u10-eyes.e5.prompt: White wants to break the eye c1. Tap the black stone White can capture.
lesson.u10-eyes.e5.hint: Which black stone has only one liberty?
lesson.u10-eyes.e5.explain: d1 has only the liberty c1; White c1 captures it.
lesson.u10-eyes.e6.prompt: The white stone on b2 makes c1 a false eye. Capture it.
lesson.u10-eyes.e6.explain: After b2 is captured both diagonals of c1 are Black's: a real eye.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.title: Two eyes live
lesson.u11-two-eyes.s1: A group with one eye dies: White fills the outside liberties, then plays inside the eye and captures.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.s2: Black b1 splits the three empty points into two eyes (两眼 liǎngyǎn): a1 and c1.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.s3: Two real eyes can never be filled: the group is alive (活 huó). One eye or none: dead (死 sǐ). That is 死活 sǐhuó.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e1.prompt: How many eyes does the marked black group have?
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e1.hint: Count the empty points enclosed by Black.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e1.explain: a1 and c1 are two real eyes.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e2.prompt: White to play. Can White capture the black group?
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e2.w2: One eye only: after White c1, a1 captures the group.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e2.explain: One eye is not enough to live.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e3.prompt: Black to play. Tap the point that makes two eyes.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e3.hint: Split the three empty points in the middle.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e3.explain: b1 leaves a1 and c1: two eyes.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e4.prompt: Black has two eyes. Tap every empty point where White may not play.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e4.hint: A white stone there would have no liberty.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e4.explain: a1 and c1 have no liberty and capture nothing.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e5.prompt: Black played a1. How many eyes does the group have now?
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e5.hint: b1 and c1 touch each other.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e5.explain: b1 and c1 are connected: one eye only.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e6.prompt: White played b1. Black to play: can Black still make two eyes?
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e6.w1: After Black a1, White c1 captures all; after Black c1, White a1 does.
lesson.u11-two-eyes.e6.explain: White b1 ruined the eye space: no second eye.
lesson.u11-vital.title: The vital point
lesson.u11-vital.s1: In a row of three empty points the middle one (b1) is the vital point (要点 yàodiǎn): whoever plays it first wins.
lesson.u11-vital.s2: If White plays b1 first, Black a1 is answered by White c1, which captures everything. No two eyes.
lesson.u11-vital.s3: A bent three works the same: the middle point a1 is vital. Black a1 makes two eyes, a2 and b1.
lesson.u11-vital.v1.prompt: Black to play and live. Tap the vital point.
lesson.u11-vital.v1.hint: Play in the middle of the three points.
lesson.u11-vital.v1.explain: b1 makes two eyes: a1 and c1.
lesson.u11-vital.v2.prompt: White to play and kill the black group.
lesson.u11-vital.v2.w1: Black b1 captures your stone and makes two eyes: alive.
lesson.u11-vital.v2.explain: b1 is the vital point: Black cannot make two eyes.
lesson.u11-vital.v3.explain: a1 makes two eyes: a2 and b1.
lesson.u11-vital.v4.prompt: White to play and kill. Tap the vital point.
lesson.u11-vital.v4.explain: a1 is the vital point: Black cannot live.
lesson.u11-vital.v5.w1: Black e1 captures your stone and makes two eyes: alive.
lesson.u11-vital.v5.explain: e1 is the vital point: Black cannot live.
lesson.u11-vital.v6.prompt: White to play. Can White kill this group?
lesson.u11-vital.v6.w1: Four in a row: whatever White plays, Black can make two eyes.
lesson.u11-vital.v6.explain: Four empty points in a row are alive.
lesson.u11-review.title: Review 3
lesson.u11-review.r1.hint: Look for an empty point enclosed by black stones.
lesson.u11-review.r1.explain: e1 is enclosed by Black: a real eye.
lesson.u11-review.r2.prompt: Is the marked point c5 a real or a false eye?
lesson.u11-review.r2.w1: White c5 captures b5, which has one liberty: a false eye.
lesson.u11-review.r2.explain: A false eye: White can capture on c5.
lesson.u11-review.r3.prompt: How many eyes does the marked black group have?
lesson.u11-review.r3.hint: Count the empty points enclosed by Black.
lesson.u11-review.r3.explain: a5 and c5 are two real eyes.
lesson.u11-review.r4.explain: c2 fills the last liberty and captures.
lesson.u11-review.r5.w1: A has no liberty and captures nothing: White may not play there.
lesson.u11-review.r5.explain: White cannot play inside a real eye.
lesson.u11-review.r6.prompt: Put the white stone in atari.
lesson.u11-review.r6.hint: It has two liberties. Fill one of them.
lesson.u11-review.r6.explain: The stone has one liberty left.
lesson.u11-review.r7.prompt: White to play and kill the black group.
lesson.u11-review.r7.hint: Play in the middle of the three points.
lesson.u11-review.r7.explain: b5 is the vital point: Black cannot live.
lesson.u11-review.r7.w1: Black b5 captures your stone and makes two eyes: alive.

fb.mark.extra.stone: Stones are not territory. Tap empty points.
fb.mark.extra.dame: {{points}} touch both colors: neutral, not territory.
fb.count.score.wrong: Not quite. Count stones and empty points separately.
fb.count.score.stonesOnly: That is only the stones. Add the territory.
fb.count.score.territoryOnly: That is only the territory. Add the stones.

lesson.u12-territory.s1: Empty points that only Black surrounds are Black's territory (地 dì). Here Black has 10 points.
lesson.u12-territory.s2: White surrounds the right column: 5 points of territory. Only empty points count, not stones.
lesson.u12-territory.s3: The middle column touches both colors. Nobody owns it: neutral points (单官 dānguān).
lesson.u12-territory.e1.hint: Look for empty points that only black stones surround.
lesson.u12-territory.e1.explain: The 5 empty points in the left column are Black's.
lesson.u12-territory.e2.hint: Black's wall closes off the bottom left.
lesson.u12-territory.e2.explain: Black surrounds 7 empty points at the bottom left.
lesson.u12-territory.e3.hint: White's wall is in the top-right.
lesson.u12-territory.e3.explain: White surrounds 7 points at the top right. The area at the bottom is Black's.
lesson.u12-territory.e4.w.black: It also touches the white stone d3, so Black alone does not surround it.
lesson.u12-territory.e4.w.white: It also touches the black stone b3.
lesson.u12-territory.e5.prompt: Tap Black's territory. Skip neutral points.
lesson.u12-territory.e5.hint: Black's territory is the left column only.
lesson.u12-territory.e5.explain: The middle column is neutral: it does not count.
lesson.u12-territory.e6.prompt: Tap Black's territory. Skip neutral points.
lesson.u12-territory.e6.hint: Two points touch a white stone: they are neutral.
lesson.u12-territory.e6.explain: d3 and e3 touch White: neutral. The other 7 points are Black's.
lesson.u12-territory.e7.hint: Count each column's empty points, then add.
lesson.u12-territory.title: Territory
lesson.u13-counting.s1: Chinese rules count area (数子 shùzǐ): your stones plus your territory. Black: 6 stones + 7 points = 13.
lesson.u13-counting.s2: White: 5 stones + 5 points = 10. The neutral points d3 and e3 count for nobody.
lesson.u13-counting.s3: Black moves first, so White gets komi (贴目 tiēmù). Here komi is 0.5: White 10.5, Black 13. Black wins by 2.5.
lesson.u13-counting.e1.prompt: How many black stones are on the board?
lesson.u13-counting.e2.prompt: How many points of Black territory? (Neutral points do not count.)
lesson.u13-counting.e2.hint: Count only empty points that Black alone surrounds.
lesson.u13-counting.e2.explain: 7 points: a1 a2 b1 b2 c1 d1 e1.
lesson.u13-counting.e4.hint: Count White's stones first, then White's territory.
lesson.u13-counting.e5.prompt: Black and White both have 10. Komi is 0.5. Who wins?
lesson.u13-counting.e6.hint: Black has 8 stones; now count the empty points below.
lesson.u13-counting.e7.prompt: White has 24. Komi is 0.5. Who wins?
lesson.u13-counting.title: Counting
lesson.u14-end.s1: When neither side has a useful move left, players pass (弃权 qìquán). Two passes in a row end the game (终局 zhōngjú).
lesson.u14-end.s2: The white stone on c1 cannot live: it is a dead stone (死子 sǐzǐ). At the end it is simply taken off the board.
lesson.u14-end.s3: Once removed, c1 is Black's territory. Black: 5 stones + 5 points = 10. White: 5 + 10 = 15.
lesson.u14-end.e5.w.black: This black wall is alive: it has room for two eyes.
lesson.u14-end.e5.w.white: This white wall is alive: lots of room above for two eyes.
lesson.u14-end.e1.w.again: Two passes in a row end the game.
lesson.u14-end.e1.prompt: Black passes, then White passes. What happens?
lesson.u14-end.e1.explain: Two passes in a row end the game. Then we count.
lesson.u14-end.e2.o.no: No: it takes two passes in a row.
lesson.u14-end.e2.w.yes: A move came between the passes.
lesson.u14-end.e2.prompt: Black passes, then White plays a stone. Is the game over?
lesson.u14-end.e2.explain: White played, so the passes were not in a row.
lesson.u14-end.e3.hint: It is alone inside Black's area.
lesson.u14-end.e3.explain: The white stone on c1 is alone in Black's area and cannot make two eyes: dead.
lesson.u14-end.e4.hint: Look for a black stone inside White's area.
lesson.u14-end.e4.explain: The black stone on c5 is trapped in White's area: dead.
lesson.u14-end.e5.hint: There is one lone stone in each area.
lesson.u14-end.e5.explain: c1 and c5 are dead; both walls are alive.
lesson.u14-end.e6.prompt: The white stone on c1 is dead. What is Black's total?
lesson.u14-end.e6.hint: Take the dead stone off: c1 is Black's territory.
lesson.u14-end.e7.prompt: c1 and c5 are dead. What is White's total?
lesson.u14-end.e7.hint: White has 5 stones plus the 10 points above.
lesson.u14-end.title: End of game and dead stones
lesson.u14-review.r1.hint: White's territory is the top row.
lesson.u14-review.r1.explain: The top row (5 points) is White's; d3 and e3 are neutral.
lesson.u14-review.r2.w.black: It also touches the white stone d4.
lesson.u14-review.r2.w.white: It also touches the black stones c3 and d2.
lesson.u14-review.r2.explain: Black and White both touch it: neutral.
lesson.u14-review.r4.hint: One row of 9 stones and 4 rows of 9 points below.
lesson.u14-review.r5.prompt: White has 36. On 9×9 komi is 7.5. Who wins?
lesson.u14-review.r6.hint: One lone stone in each area.
lesson.u14-review.r6.explain: c1 and c5 are dead; the walls are alive.
lesson.u14-review.r7.prompt: c1 and c5 are dead. Komi is 0.5. Who wins?
lesson.u14-review.r7.hint: Take the dead stones off first, then count both sides.
